notes:
Summary: focused procurement for Redwood Dedicated. Primary ask: contractual throughput guarantees + clear burst policy. 

Recent timeline:
- 2025-11-05: initial intro call (discovery) w/ AE Maya Chen, SE Daniel Park. Business case: low-latency chat for trader desk + semantic search for internal documents.
- 2025-12-10: architecture deep-dive with infra + security (VPC, KMS). Recorded ff-20251210-security (link in Drive).

POC / technical findings (key metrics):
- Baseline single A100-80GB (fp16) observed ~12k tokens/sec for long-context chat (1k avg seq) when batching aggressively.
- With H100 + int8 quantization path projected ~28-32k tokens/sec per GPU for chat workload.
- Embedding precompute (384-d) throughput dominated by batching — up to ~2000 reqs/s on 4x GPUs when using async batching.
- KV-cache hit improved tail latency by ~40% for repeated session traffic.

Aurora's requirements / negotiation asks (explicit):
- Contracted minimum sustained throughput: 120k tokens/sec across the dedicated pool during business hours (08:00-20:00 ET).
- Concurrency cap expectations: sustained concurrency 250 simultaneous chat sessions, p95 latency <= 350ms for short-turn prompts (<128 tokens).
- Burst policy: allow elastic bursts up to 400k tokens/sec for up to 2 minutes, with 6-hour replenishment window (burst credits) — customer willing to pay for reserved burst capacity.
- Reserved GPU planning: target initial reservation of 8x H100-equivalent; plan to scale to 16 within 6 months if SLAs met. Support for mixed instance types (H100 + A100) acceptable with performance accounting.
- Model preferences: primaries are a 30-70B family (quantized int8) with fallback to a 13B variant for heavy-burst degradation. Routing policy must support instantaneous fallback and consistent token accounting.

Negotiation points / Redwood asks & tradeoffs discussed:
- Redwood proposed SLO: guaranteed minimum 100k tokens/sec with burst to 350k tokens/sec; Aurora pushing for 120k sustained.
- Concurrency vs tokens/sec: Redwood asks for cap on concurrent sessions if customers want higher sustained tokens/sec guarantees. Aurora requested soft cap of 300 sessions with graceful degradation policy (fallback to smaller model) rather than hard rejects.
- Billing model: reserved capacity base + overage for sustained bursts. Aurora prefers fixed monthly commit for predictable ARR.
- Monitoring & penalties: Aurora requires token-level telemetry + monthly SLA credit schedule; Redwood requested 30-day notice for major infra changes.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must support SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation, KMS integration; data residency requirement for NA only. Security team requested Redwood security FAQ and architecture diagram (in Drive).

Open action items (working):
- Redwood to produce formal throughput guarantee proposal with metric definitions (tokens/sec window, measurement agent, p95 calculation) by 2026-02-22.
- Aurora legal to provide redlined SLA by 2026-02-26.
- SE to schedule 4-hour ramp test: synthetic load + realistic user replay to validate token/sec and burst behavior (target date 2026-03-03).
- Infra to confirm availability of 8x H100-equivalent in us-east1 reserved pool for start date 2026-04-01.
